topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the course topic on cancer causation and outlines the main learning objectives of the lecture.

topics.label: Cancer Etiology: Endogenous Factors, Environmental Exposures, and Epidemiology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics introduce the fundamental drivers of cancer development, examining the interaction between endogenous biological processes, environmental exposures, and global epidemiological patterns.

topics.label: Infectious Pathogens and Cancer Development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how infectious agents drive oncogenesis, focusing in detail on the multi-step pathogenesis of Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Chemical and Physical Mutagens and Mechanisms of DNA Damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the molecular mechanisms by which dietary, environmental, and chemical mutagens undergo physical or metabolic activation to induce DNA adducts and mutations.

topics.label: Tumour Promotion, Host Susceptibility, and Mechanisms of Carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine non-mutagenic tumour promotion, host developmental and tissue susceptibilities, and summarize the diverse mechanisms driving malignant transformation.

topics.label: Methods for Identifying and Testing Carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the genomic, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro methodologies used to determine and validate the carcinogenicity of environmental agents.

topics.label: Conclusion and Risk-Benefit Analysis
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the session by reflecting on personal risk-benefit assessments regarding carcinogen exposure and providing closing summary remarks.
